title: The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct: Start Time, How To Watch, And What To Expect
description: Can you believe that The Legend of Zelda franchise turned 40 this year? It's true, and it's the main focus of today's new Nintendo Direct. The series is in the spotlight, and Nintendo says it'll celebrate its ruby anniversary with a new broadcast that fans will want to check out. Don't forget, there'll also be a Nintendo Direct on September 9, but for now, here's a closer look at how you can watch the Zelda stream. How to watch the Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct As usual, you can watch the Legend of Zelda Nintendo Direct on YouTube and Twitch. Once the livestream wraps up, Nintendo typically uploads individual versions of the trailers and footage shown off, all available to watch on its official YouTube page. YouTube Twitch Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct start time Kicking off early on September 8 at 7 AM PT / 10 AM ET, this Legend of Zelda Direct will run for around 30 minutes. 7 AM PT 10 AM ET 3 PM BST 4 PM CEST 11 PM JST What to expect from the Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct Nintendo says the presentation will deliver "a variety of information" related to The Legend of Zelda. Beyond that, your guess is as good as ours, but we expect to see a new look at the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, with a closer look at its gameplay, how it differs from the classic Nintendo 64 game, and its release date. A teaser for the upcoming live-action movie ahead of its 2027 release would also be welcome, and if we had to take an educated guess, we'd expect 40th-anniversary limited-edition hardware for the Switch 2, more merchandise drops, and maybe even concert tour celebrations. And if we're really lucky, maybe we'll finally get an update on two outstanding Legend of Zelda ports: Wind Waker HD and Twilight Princess HD. Considering how Nintendo has brought other Legend of Zelda adventures into the modern era, it's high time that these classics made their way to Switch consoles.

title: The Best Tabletop Role-Playing Games To Play That Aren’t Dungeons & Dragons
description: Tabletop role-playing games have reached an all-time high in popularity. Turns out, there’s a certain appeal about rounding up a group of friends together to go through an adventure while chucking dice in the process. For over half a century, the juggernaut of the genre has been none other than Dungeons & Dragons, designed by Gary Gygax and made super-popular through Critical Role, Stranger Things, multiple feature films, and countless other media. While the latest iteration of the fantastic game might be the best it's been in years, you're missing out if you haven't stopped to consider its alternatives. Whether you're looking for a lighter rules systems, different settings, or an entirely different concept, there has never been a better time to explore other RPG systems. Here’s a quick rundown of a few of the best out there. Mork Borg Have you ever felt that D&D was getting a bit too cozy? Maybe the sometimes-crunchy rules for combat drag down the flow of the game. Maybe you just want to roll up a complete scumbag of a character and D&D’s ruleset don’t really facilitate that. Well, Mork Borg just might be for you! A rules-lite system that owes more to the Old School Renaissance (OSR) movement of RPG design that aims to recreate rules similar to the original editions of D&D, Mork Borg puts a unique spin on setting and atmosphere. Inspired by the extreme tone of Doom Metal album covers and music, the game has players roll up a scumbag of a character with little hope of surviving in a doomed plane. I'd highly recommend it to fans of the dark fantasy genre, Darkest Dungeon, and other grim games. However, if fantasy's not your bag, give its spin-off Cy_Borg a try, as it amps up the violence and chaos of a game like Cyberpunk 2077 to 11. AMC’s The Walking Dead: The Role-Playing Game Okay, hear me out. I know the years haven’t been kind to The Walking Dead television series or its ungodly amount of spin-offs, but I found myself thoroughly impressed with this rule system.…

title: Blood Dungeon Is A Survivors-Like For People Who Don’t Like Vampire Survivors
description: Not everybody bought into Vampire Survivors. The 2021 game popularized the idea of "bullet heaven," a reversal of elements normally seen in "bullet hell" games, and made such a huge impact on the industry that some call this subgenre "Survivors-likes." But while Vampire Survivors was a giant leap, it wasn't a wholly satisfying one for some. Blood Dungeon, a new "bullet hell" from Nidhogg and Wheel World developer Messhof, runs with some of the ideas that made Survivors a hit, fleshing them out and helping define the future of the genre Vampire Survivors sired. The chief hallmarks of a "Survivors-like" are automatic combat, hordes of enemies that get stronger with every wave, and the kind of randomized upgrades found in roguelikes. You see it in Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor, Brotato, and 20 Minutes Till Dawn, and there's even a Breakout-inspired brick-busting riff called Ball X Pit. The RPG-style progression acts like a hook to keep you playing, but the fundamental passivity of their indirect combat, and the inherent unpredictability and impermanence of those upgrades, can be off-putting. And Vampire Survivors itself has an aesthetic that overtly evokes Castlevania, with very similar artwork and environments, which makes it look a little uninspired. Sorry, pal. But you're never beating the Castlevania accusations. I know not everybody bought into Vampire Survivors, because I didn't really myself. I had a fixation with it for a short spell in 2022, and still find it preferable to many of the games inspired by it, but ultimately it's about as hollow as its biggest critics allege. If any game can be called a "walking simulator," it's this one, as walking is all you do--moving left, right, up, and down, with no tactility or physical friction--just endless swarms of monsters desperate to mulch you up as you glide around its wide-open, top-down levels. Its whole personality feels canned, prefab, as interchangeable as its Konami-aping art. Good for its developer that they…

title: New horror game The Well Is Not Empty combines photophobic monsters with timer light switches and a lot of frenzied digging
description: "Never show the monster," horror film-makers, game-makers and other creepozoids have chanted, over the decades. The Well Is Not Empty wastes no time showing us the monster - one of the monsters, at least - and doesn't seem especially the worse for it. I mean, it's the worse, but in a good way. Look, you can see the monster right there, hunkered up like a frightened puppy in the corner of the room. A scrawny little fellow with broken xylophone teeth and eyes that genuinely do make me think of the view from the bottom of a well. The monster is no threat, as long as you stay out of grabbing distance - and as long as the lights are on. The problem, as you've already guessed, is that the lights are unreliable. A lot of the ceiling bulbs in the open areas are set to a timer. Best make sure you're back behind the sturdy radiance of those construction lamps before the ticking stops. Read more

title: Combat and socially agonised teens impress in Persona 4 Revival, the RPG that series director Kazuhisa Wada feels a "duty" to make
description: Look, before you say it, I know. Persona 4 Golden is held up by some as one of the best and most important RPGs ever. After all, it was the series' Final Fantasy 7 moment, where many of the mechanical and thematic threads of the earlier games finally knitted together and became something greater than their parts. You step into the shoes of Yu Narukami, a Japanese transfer student freshly arrived in Inaba. There, you use your limited time to make friends, study for your exams, and dive into a metaphysical dimension to turn-based battle the literal manifestations of your friends and rivals' twisted perceptions of themselves. Its story and characters particularly celebrated for their honest and painful looks inward at the parts of ourselves best left unseen. I’m a fraud for not having played it yet, with that sin only compounded by having had it in my Steam family sharing library for years. I have no excuse. I’ll face the shame-filled shadow version of myself, eventually. Read more

title: "We believe in the power of connection": Donald Trump Tetris parody game rouses the mildly worded wrath of the Tetris Company
description: Those terrible firebrands at the Tetris Company have publicly rebuked the US government for publishing a Tetris parody game that promotes the Trump administration's brutalising rhetoric about securing the border with Mexico. They've even hinted that they're prepared to sue over it. The parody game in question is called Build the Wall, and sees you stacking bricks along "the Southern border" in order to repel invading zombies. Unlike in regular Tetris - yes, I've played the Trump game, I'm definitely going to hell now - you aren't trying to clear lines of blocks. Instead, blocks defeat wandering undead of the same colour. The game appeared last week alongside a swathe of other Trumpist propaganda games, based on the likes of Snake and Flappy Bird. A few of these games include goofy reworkings of Sony, Nintendo and Xbox console logo screens. The three platform holders have yet to comment. But the Tetris Company? They're coming out swinging with a... gently worded appeal to human community. Read more

title: Get The Entire Metro Series For Under $9 Ahead Of Metro 2039’s Release
description: While I’m a fan of the Stalker games, there’s something about the more linear nature and, ironically, on-rails experience that the Metro games deliver. With a tense atmosphere, mutated creatures, and factions split within the underground of a demolished Russia, the Metro series might be some of my favorite FPS games of all time—and with Metro 2039 almost here, now’s the chance to catch up on the series for less than $9. That’s all three of the games released so far. The series starts with Metro 2033, two decades after an apocalyptic event ended most of mankind and turned the surface into a radioactive wasteland. Even breathing the air is enough to kill you, but the monstrous creatures above will do that far quicker. You play as Artyom, who leaves the safety of his home station in order to warn the rest of the metro about a new, mysterious mutant threat called the Dark Ones. I can’t really go into more detail on Metro Last Light without spoiling the predecessor. So, just take my word for it: it is arguably better, with a great narrative bolstered by gameplay improvements. Metro Exodus follows Artyom as he believes life still continues outside of Moscow, and aboard the Aurora train alongside his wife and the Spartan Rangers, he heads off to discover the truth. In all three of the Metro games, you’re limited to a first-person view, putting you face-to-face with enemies of the human and mutant variety. Even though it may look like your typical FPS game, there’s a lot more of a survival focus, with limited resources meaning that every bullet needs to count, and using your gas mask’s filters at the right time is essential to surviving. All three Metro games are the remastered or enhanced editions with this discount. In fact, Exodus is actually the version that includes all post-launch DLC, so you’re getting the entire Metro series so far at a very steep discount, right as the Metro 2039 release date has been announced. If you’re looking to give it a try, you can grab the…

title: See Ripped Game Of Thrones Actor’s Pitch To Play God Of War’s Kratos In Role Already Cast By Another Ripped Actor
description: God of War fans have been on a rollercoaster ride recently while waiting for the TV show adaptation to come to life. After originally casting Ryan Hurst for the role, Amazon was forced to find another suitably ripped actor after Hurst was horrifically injured on set. Last week his replacement, Dave Bautista, showed off his transformation so far for the role. Now, though, Game of Thrones actor Hafþór Júlíus Björnsson, or Thor Bjornsson, who played The Mountain in the HBO series, has shared an image depicting him as Kratos, asking fans if they'd like to see him take on the role. Posting on X, Bjornsson captioned the image, "Be honest... would you guys want to see me as Kratos?" The image, likely generated by AI, shows the ripped actor in an even more ripped state, dressed in Kratos' attire, complete with his trademark red tattoo, inked to honor his brother, Deimos. Of course, with Bautista already cast, Bjornsson's desire to portray Kratos is merely a wish, and isn't likely to come to fruition, but it's fun to see the towering 6 foot 9 Icelandic strongman looking like a Spartan warrior. Several other actors have expressed a desire to play the role, including Christopher Judge, the game's original voice actor. However, he's pretty frustrated that TV show adaptations regularly fail to hire anyone that worked on the source material. The God of War TV show is expected to resume production in late October or early November, although there's no estimated release date for the series just yet.
